Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk on Thursday wasn’t having it with President Donald Trump’s welcoming words to Russian President Vladimir Putin in China.

Trump — ahead of his summit with Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen — asked, “Who is he?” while pointing at Putin from across the room before chuckling and answering himself, “He’s my friend!” The two then shook hands, and Trump told Putin, “Nice to see you.”

Tusk — who leads the NATO-allied nation that borders both Russia and Ukraine — is one of a number of European officials set to meet with Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner for peace talks Thursday in Berlin.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, unlike the summit in China that he wasn’t invited to attend, is expected to attend the talks in Germany.

Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski, like Tusk, expressed concern over Trump’s chummy exchange with Putin, per The Guardian.

“Because the question arises – who is he more of a friend with, Putin or our president? And what will he possibly do if push comes to shove, which friend will he choose?” he wondered aloud.
